title: Unveiling Synergetic Photocatalytic Activity from Heterometallic Ti/Ce Clusters

synthesis.procedure: Dissolve cerium nitrate hexahydrate and benzoic acid in acetonitrile and stir at 500 rpm for 30 min. Add titanium isopropoxide dropwise, stir for another 5 min, then heat at 80 °C for 18 h. Wash the resulting crystals with acetonitrile and acetone and vacuum-dry at 120 °C for at least 8 h.
synthesis.time: 30 min initial stirring, 5 min after titanium addition, 18 h heating, and at least 8 h drying
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Stirred solution followed by oven heating
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Large yellowish leaf-shaped crystals; wash with acetonitrile and acetone, then vacuum-dry.
synthesis.yield: Approximately 100 mg; approximately 32 wt % based on added Ce

properties.summary: Light absorption, an optical band gap, and photoluminescence were investigated. This cluster had the highest photoluminescence intensity of the three reported Ti/Ce clusters.

measurements.name: Optical band gap
measurements.conditions: From the reported Tauc-plot and band-position analysis

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The single-crystal structure contains two Ce(IV) and eight Ti(IV) centers arranged as a bicapped tetragonal prism, linked by benzoates and bridging oxo groups.

synthesis.procedure: Prepare the 1 g-scale Ti8Ce2(BA)16 reaction mixture from cerium nitrate hexahydrate and benzoic acid in acetonitrile, followed by dropwise titanium isopropoxide addition and heating. Filter off Ti8Ce2(BA)16 and return its filtrate to an 80 °C oven for 24 h to obtain Ti9Ce4(BA)20 powder. Wash with acetonitrile and acetone and vacuum-dry at 120 °C for at least 8 h. For single crystals, add benzoic acid to the filtrate until saturated and heat at 100 °C.

synthesis.temperature: 60 °C for the initial 1 g-scale reaction; 80 °C for powder formation; 100 °C for single-crystal growth; 120 °C during vacuum-drying
synthesis.time: 120 min initial stirring, 15 min after titanium addition, 8 h initial heating, 24 h filtrate heating for powder, and at least 8 h drying
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Heated filtrate from the 1 g-scale Ti8Ce2(BA)16 synthesis
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filter off the initial Ti8Ce2(BA)16 product. Wash the subsequently formed Ti9Ce4(BA)20 powder with acetonitrile and acetone and vacuum-dry. Benzoic-acid-saturated filtrate yields dark-yellow block-shaped single crystals upon heating.
synthesis.yield: Approximately 14.5 wt % based on the Ce remaining in the filtrate

properties.summary: Light absorption and photoluminescence were reported. Its photoluminescence intensity was lower than that of Ti8Ce2(BA)16 but higher than that of TiCe-BA.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The single-crystal structure contains nine Ti and four Ce centers in a low-symmetry oxo-bridged core with 20 coordinated benzoates. Two acetonitrile molecules cocrystallize with the cluster.

material_class.structural_family: Titanium–cerium oxo benzoate cluster; structure not determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction

synthesis.procedure: Prepare and heat the 1 g-scale Ti8Ce2(BA)16 reaction mixture, then filter off that product. Leave the filtrate at room temperature until TiCe-BA precipitates. Wash the product with acetonitrile and acetone and vacuum-dry at 120 °C for at least 8 h. For crystal growth, add excess benzoic acid to saturate the filtrate and leave it at room temperature.

Excess benzoic acid in the filtrate yielded small dark-yellow square plates, but these did not permit single-crystal structure determination.
